@@CASE@@: Fig.~\ref{fig:case} shows two patterns on D4 at the threshold of $K=300$ ($\gamma=0.0017$) with the same point score, 0.0041. Blue points have positive and orange points negative posterior means, and fainter points have larger variances. The kept pattern \{Chinese restaurant, food and drink shop, salon/barbershop\} rests on 18 venues with a median of 5.5 training check-ins, and its lower bound is 0.0035. The rejected pattern \{bar, salon/barbershop\} rests on 329 venues with a median of two training check-ins, whose posterior variances add up to 184. Its lower bound is therefore 0.0010 with independent variances, already below $\gamma$, and falls to 0.0005 once the error of the estimated prior and center, shared by these venues, raises the variance to 245 (Definition~\ref{def:totalvar}). The variance of the kept pattern stays near 8.
@@EFFTEXT@@: Fig.~\ref{fig:eff} shows the mining time on D4 and D5, and Table~\ref{tab:ablation} the ablation. With $k=20$ features the pattern space is small (3,481 nodes on D4), and a bound evaluation costs about as much as the nodes it saves. At $K=300$, UHUCPM evaluates 38\% of the nodes of NoPrune on D4 in the same time, and at $K=1000$ it is slower than NoPrune on D4 and no faster on D5. The space grows exponentially with $k$ while the patterns above the threshold do not, so the bounds pay off as $k$ grows. At $k=80$ and $K=100$, UHUCPM evaluates 4.0\% and 0.56\% of the nodes of NoPrune on D4 and D5 and takes 1.9\,s against 18\,s and 53\,s against 1,274\,s. A lower threshold has the opposite effect, because it enlarges the part of the space that no bound can prune (Fig.~\ref{fig:eff}(a), (b)). The suffix bound matters most. Without it, UHUCPM evaluates 1.34 and 1.82 times as many nodes on D4 and D5, and a linear scan of the suffix bounds instead of the binary search takes 30\% and 12\% more time. At $z=1.645$ the exact bound evaluates about 9\% fewer nodes than the mean bound at a similar time, because the variance penalty is still small. It pays off at larger $z$. At $z=3.09$ ($\delta=0.001$) and $k=60$, it evaluates 18\% and 19\% fewer nodes on D4 and D5 and takes 11\% and 12\% less time.
